thread.title: Survey Shows Strong Demand For iPhone XS, Apple Watch Series 4 | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Survey Shows Strong Demand For iPhone XS, Apple Watch Series 4 | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Survey results out Wednesday pointed to strong consumer demand for Apple 's ( AAPL ) just-released iPhone XS handsets and Apple Watch Series 4 smartwatches.
X RBC Capital Markets polled 5,280 U.S. consumers last week about their purchase plans. The survey results indicated a preference for more expensive models of Apple's 12th-generation smartphones. The poll also showed greater interest in Apple's smartwatches and AirPods wireless earbuds.
Based on the survey results, RBC analyst Amit Daryanani raised his price target on Apple stock to 250 from 240. He reiterated his outperform rating.
Apple dipped 0.8% to close at 220.42 on the stock market today .

Please contact customer service CLOSE "We think demand for this generation iPhones — XS Max/XS/XR — is robust and ASPs (average selling prices) and gross margins could improve given (sales) mix benefits," Daryanani said in a note to clients.
IPhone XS Max Is The Most Popular Apple began selling its iPhone XS and XS Max handsets last Friday. The devices have OLED displays measuring 5.8 and 6.5 inches, respectively. The midrange iPhone XR, which has a 6.1-inch LCD screen, goes on sales Oct. 26. The iPhone XS starts at $999, while the XS Max starts at $1,099. The iPhone XR starts at $749.
Among prospective buyers surveyed by RBC, the high-end iPhone XS Max is the most popular model. It is the choice of 25% of customers surveyed.
"This is a bit surprising given iPhone XS Max pricing," he said.
The iPhone XS came in second with 20% of prospective buyers, followed by 12% for the iPhone XR. The rest of likely buyers chose older models. The iPhone 7 and 8 series handsets are available now at lower prices.
Consumers also indicated a preference for pricier models with more flash memory for storing photos, video and other data. That "should further enhance ASPs and gross margins," Daryanani said.
More People Planning To Buy iPhones This Cycle Overall, iPhone purchase intentions increased from last year. Among consumers surveyed, 26% plan to buy a new iPhone this cycle vs. 20% a year ago.
"Despite high ASPs this year, iPhone volumes are likely to be healthy this cycle," Daryanani said.
In addition to the preference for premium iPhone models, another surprise from the survey results was strong demand for the Apple Watch and AirPods.
"Our survey results indicate that consumer interest in the Apple Watch is significantly higher vs. past levels, with 26% of prospective iPhone buyers interested in purchasing it vs. 13% last year," Daryanani said. "We also note that 29% of respondents intend to buy AirPods and 19% already own them."
